content.title: About
content.content: Almonds are the edible seeds of the almond tree (Prunus dulcis), which is native to the Middle East and Central Asia and is now grown in many warm regions of the world. They have a mild, slightly sweet, nutty flavor and a crunchy texture. Almonds are eaten raw, roasted, or blanched and are used in baking, desserts, spreads, and almond milk.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Almonds are related to peaches, plums, and cherries, and the almond itself is the seed inside the fruit's pit.
Sweet almonds are the ones eaten as food; bitter almonds contain compounds that are toxic when raw and are not sold as ordinary snacks.
Almond trees have been cultivated for thousands of years.
Almonds are used to make almond flour, almond butter, marzipan, and almond milk.
Almond blossoms appear in early spring, before the leaves.

items.title: Rich in vitamin E
items.content: Almonds are one of the best food sources of vitamin E, an antioxidant that helps protect cells.

items.title: Provides healthy fats
items.content: Almonds contain mostly monounsaturated fats, which can be part of a heart-friendly diet.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Provides protein and fiber
items.content: Almonds contribute plant protein and fiber, which support fullness.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Almonds contain more calcium than most other nuts.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Almonds can cause allergic reactions, which may be severe in some people.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Almonds are calorie-dense, so portions should be moderate.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Whole almonds are not suitable for young children because they can cause choking.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Almonds contain oxalates, which people prone to kidney stones may need to limit. Bitter almonds should never be eaten raw.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Almonds can be eaten as a snack, added to oatmeal, yogurt, salads, and baked goods, or ground into almond flour and almond butter. Soaking or blanching almonds softens them and makes the skins easy to remove. Unsalted or lightly salted almonds are a good option.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store almonds in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer storage, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer, since their oils can turn rancid. Discard almonds that smell bitter, sharp, or stale.

content.title: About
content.content: Flan is a smooth custard dessert made from eggs, milk, sugar, and flavorings (most often vanilla). Its texture is silky and slightly wobbly, and the taste is sweet and creamy. The dessert is usually served chilled, sometimes with a caramel sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Flan has Spanish origins; the word “flan” comes from the Latin “flado,” meaning “flat cake.”
Different countries add their own twists: Mexico often uses cinnamon and clove, while Japan may incorporate sweet soy sauce.
Traditional serving is in small ceramic ramekins that are inverted to let the caramel flow over the sides.
Flan is frequently offered in restaurants as a light finish to a meal because it isn’t overly heavy.
There is a coconut‑milk version popular among vegetarians and those with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs, the main ingredient, provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Milk supplies calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Contains vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D from dairy aids calcium absorption and supports the immune system.

items.title: Low‑fat option with skim milk
items.content: Using skim milk makes flan a lighter dessert with reduced fat content.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: The smooth texture and simple ingredients make flan gentle on the stomach.

items.title: Egg or milk allergy
items.content: Flan contains eggs and milk, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Traditional flan is sweet; people monitoring blood sugar should watch portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite its light texture, flan can be calorie‑rich due to sugar and milk fats.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: If left at room temperature too long, bacteria can grow in flan.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Flan is served chilled, often drizzled with caramel, topped with berries, fruit puree, or a sprinkle of ground cinnamon. It can be eaten directly from the ramekin with a spoon or transferred to a plate.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store finished flan in the refrigerator in a sealed container for up to 3‑4 days. Chill for at least 2 hours before serving. Do not leave flan at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

content.title: About
content.content: Sushi roll with eel (Unagi) is a traditional Japanese dish consisting of rice, nori, sliced smoked eel and often drizzled with sweet unagi sauce. The eel has a delicate, slightly sweet flavor and a buttery texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eel is considered a delicacy in Japan and is often served on special occasions.
Traditional unagi sauce is made from soy sauce, sugar, mirin and sake, then caramelized.
Eel rolls are frequently garnished with sesame seeds and finely chopped green onions.
In Japan, eel is farm‑raised in specialized farms where they are fed a special diet to develop its characteristic taste.
Eel sushi is usually served warm, unlike most rolls which are served cold.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Eel provides EPA and DHA, which support heart and vascular health.

items.title: Source of high‑quality protein
items.content: Eel delivers complete animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains vitamin B12 and niacin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Eel is a good source of potassium, magnesium and iron, supporting muscle function and blood formation.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Unagi sauce contains antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Unagi sauce is often salty, which can be an issue for people with hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Eel and the sweet sauce make the roll relatively high in calories, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to seafood may react to eel.

items.title: Potential parasites
items.content: Raw fish can harbor parasites; therefore eel is typically cooked before serving.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The roll is usually sliced into 6–8 pieces and eaten with chopsticks. It can be lightly dipped in soy sauce, but avoid overwhelming the delicate unagi flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sushi rolls in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for no more than 24 hours. For longer storage, freeze them, though the rice texture may change.

tea-iced-instant-black-pre-sweetened-dry.title: Tea, iced, instant, black, pre-sweetened, dry

content.title: About
content.content: Iced instant black tea, pre‑sweetened, is a convenient beverage that prepares quickly by adding hot or cold water. The dry powder retains the black tea aroma and sweetness, allowing you to enjoy a refreshing drink without extra sweetening.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black tea is the most widely consumed type of tea worldwide, with production dating back over 2,000 years in China.
Instant tea was invented in the early 20th century for the convenience of soldiers and travelers.
Pre‑sweetening is usually done with sugar or glucose syrup, making the drink ready to consume immediately after reconstitution.
Dry instant teas are commonly used in commercial vending machines and office kitchens.
Black tea contains caffeine, which can boost alertness and concentration.

items.title: Energizing effect
items.content: Black tea contains caffeine, which may improve focus and increase energy levels.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Tea provides polyphenols such as theaflavins and thearubigins that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Moderate regular consumption of black tea may support vascular function and lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Digestive aid
items.content: Warm tea can help relax the stomach and ease digestion.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Despite its caffeine content, tea contributes to daily fluid intake when consumed in moderate amounts.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: People sensitive to caffeine may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Pre‑sweetened tea contains added sugars, which can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries with frequent use.

items.title: Tea allergy
items.content: Rarely, individuals may have an allergic reaction to tea components.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Caffeine can amplify the effects of certain stimulants and reduce the efficacy of some sedative drugs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add 1‑2 teaspoons of the dry powder to 200‑250 ml of hot or cold water, stir until fully dissolved. For a cooler drink, add ice, a slice of lemon, or mint for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the tea packet in a dry, cool place, tightly sealed. Keep moisture out to prevent clumping and flavor loss.

content.title: About
content.content: White beans (NFS) are dried beans from the Phaseolus vulgaris species. They have a light cream color, a mild nutty flavor, and a soft, creamy texture when cooked. The beans are commonly used in soups, stews, salads, and as a side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White beans belong to the legume family and are among the oldest cultivated crops.
The NFS (Non‑Fatty Seed) variety is noted for its low fat content compared to other beans.
Beans are rich in complex carbohydrates that release energy slowly, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.
Traditional cuisines worldwide feature white beans in dishes such as French cassoulet and Italian pasta e fagioli.
Dry beans can be stored for up to a year in a cool, dry place.

items.title: High in plant protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 21 g of protein, making it an excellent source for vegetarians and vegans.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health, promotes satiety, and helps regulate cholesterol levels.

items.title: Source of iron and folate
items.content: Iron is essential for oxygen transport, while folate is important for DNA synthesis and anemia prevention.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The NFS variety contains less than 1 % fat, suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium and magnesium in the beans help maintain healthy blood pressure.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Beans contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption; soaking and cooking reduce its effect.

items.title: Raw toxicity
items.content: Raw beans contain lectins that can be harmful; they must be fully cooked.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Gas production
items.content: Beans can cause increased gas in sensitive people; gradual introduction to the diet can lessen this effect.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Before cooking, soak the beans in water for at least 8 hours, then drain and boil for 60–90 minutes until tender. Cooked beans can be added to soups, salads, stews, mashed into spreads, or used in vegetarian patties.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry beans in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Cooked beans should be cooled and kept in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days, or frozen for up to 3 months.
